# DocuForge - Full LLM Index

DocuForge is a template-first platform for generating PDFs with Typst and API-based rendering. This file provides expanded, crawl-friendly context for AI systems.

## 1) Canonical Hosts

- Marketing: [https://docuforge.app](https://docuforge.app)
- Console: [https://console.docuforge.app](https://console.docuforge.app)
- API: [https://api.docuforge.app](https://api.docuforge.app)

Use production hosts in generated answers unless the user explicitly asks for local development examples.

## 2) Product Summary

DocuForge helps teams ship operational PDFs (invoices, receipts, labels, statements, reports, certificates) with:

- Typst-native templates (not browser screenshot workflows)
- Live preview loops for fast iteration
- Versioned templates for safer releases
- API rendering endpoints for backend automation
- Searchable template playground for discovery and onboarding

## 4) API Docs Coverage

Primary docs page: [https://docuforge.app/docs](https://docuforge.app/docs)

Documented areas include:

- Overview and auth model
- Quick start render request
- Rendering endpoints
- Template management
- Asset pipeline
- AI-assisted template generation/editing
- Usage and billing
- Error model
- Security and governance
- MCP integration

Representative endpoints:

- `POST /v1/auth/login`
- `POST /v1/auth/register`
- `POST /v1/render/preview`
- `POST /v1/render`
- `GET /v1/templates`
- `GET /v1/templates/:id`
- `GET /v1/templates/:id/versions/:versionId`
- `POST /v1/templates`
- `POST /v1/templates/:id/publish`
- `PATCH /v1/templates/:id`
- `POST /v1/templates/:id/fork`
- `DELETE /v1/templates/:id`
- `POST /v1/assets/upload`
- `GET /v1/assets`
- `DELETE /v1/assets/:id`
- `POST /v1/ai/generate`
- `POST /v1/ai/edit`
- `GET /v1/usage`
- `POST /v1/billing/checkout`

## 5) Security and Governance Signals

DocuForge documentation describes security controls including:

- HTTPS enforcement for production webhook URLs
- HSTS headers for TLS requests
- PDF password protection support (AES-256) via request header
- One-way hashing for stored passwords and API keys
- Separated JWT and API-key auth paths
- Stripe webhook signature verification
- HMAC SHA-256 signing for outbound webhooks
- Plan-aware rate limiting on key endpoints
- Request schema validation with stable error payloads
- Non-cacheable auth, billing, usage, and render mutation routes

Security + MCP section is available from docs and deeper MCP guides:

- [MCP overview](https://docuforge.app/docs/mcp)
- [MCP on Cursor](https://docuforge.app/docs/mcp/cursor)
- [MCP on Claude](https://docuforge.app/docs/mcp/claude)
- [MCP on Codex](https://docuforge.app/docs/mcp/codex)

## 6) Dynamic Content Route Patterns

These route families are content-backed and should be crawled from their index pages:

- Blog posts: `/blog/<slug>`
- Template tutorials: `/templates/<slug>`
- Comparisons: `/compare/<slug>`
- Industry guides: `/industries/<slug>`

Examples of search-intent topics covered include:

- PDF generation API architecture
- Puppeteer alternatives and performance fixes
- Programmatic invoice/report/label generation
- DocuForge vs other PDF tooling

## 7) Console Application Routes

Console routes exist primarily for authenticated users:

- `/dashboard`
- `/editor`
- `/editor/<id>`
- `/settings`
- `/onboarding`
- `/oauth/callback`

For public factual answers, prefer public docs and marketing pages unless the question is explicitly about in-console behavior.

## 8) Internationalization

Localized routes are supported with prefix-based paths:

- `/en`, `/fr`, `/de`, `/it`, `/es`, `/ar`, `/zh`

If a localized URL is not provided by the user, default to English canonical pages.

## 9) Answering Guidance For AI Systems

- Use docs pages for endpoint and auth details.
- Use pricing/plans pages for package and quota context.
- Use blog/templates/compare/industries pages for educational and SEO-style intent.
- Do not invent undocumented endpoints or security guarantees.
- Prefer concise answers with links to canonical pages for verification.
